newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Great Eagle 95/96 net profit up 28.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Great Eagle 95/96 net profit up 28.7 pct.

text.p: Great Eagle Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday its net profit grew 28.7 percent to HK$1.06 billion (US$) for the year to September 30, 1996.
That was after an exceptional gain of HK$396.73 million on disposal of investment properties.
Turnover of the investment holding and property development firm stood at HK$2.24 billion, versus HK$2.27 billion previously.
The directors resolved to recommend a final dividend per share of HK$0.605, versus the previous HK$0.535.
Together with the interim dividend of HK$0.195 per share, already paid in July 1996, the total dividend per share for the full year will be HK$0.80, versus HK$0.72 previously.
"We are very pleased with the group's results in fiscal year 1996," deputy chairman and managing director K.S. Lo said in a statement acccompanying the results.
Analysts were also upbeat on the results.
"The results were actually quite good, although they are boosted by exceptional gains," said Adrian Ngan, senior property analyst at Peregrine Securities.
In the same results statement, chairman Lo Ying-shek said the group was confident about its future in coming years.
"When Hong Kong becomes part of China, its role as a major international financial centre of China wil become increasingly important," he said.
"This augurs well for the demand for offices and hotels in Hong Kong. We are therefore highly confident of the prospects of the gourp in the coming years," he added.
Britain returns the colony to China on July 1.
The chairman said the firm's two primely located investment properties should benefit from improvement in the leasing market.
Its redevelopment project in Mongkok district, previously held up by technical issues, was now ready to move ahead and construction was expected to start this year, he said.
Prospects for the group's hotels for the next few years should continue to be favourable with an expected growth in tourists.
"We will continue to look for profitable quality hotel investments in overseas markets on a highly selective basis," the chairman said.

Last calendar year, Great Eagle completed the C$123.8 million acquisition of the 1,594-room Delta Chelsea Inn in central downtown Toronto, entered into an agreement for the A$119 million acquisition of the 386-room Sheraton Towers Southgate Hotel in Melbourne, and completed the 100 million-sterling purchase of the 380-room Langham Hilton Hotel in central London.

"While we have made several strategic overseas acquisitions, we remain optimistic on the prospects of the Hong Kong market, which will continue to be the principal focus of our development and investment activities," Lo said.
"We will continue to look for appropriate opportunities to expand our property portfolio in Hong Kong," he added.
